missing_evidence: No documentation resolving or explaining the duplicate invoice submission (INV-1003-A and INV-1003-B share identical amount, date, and reference SSS/2026/188) - absent a credit note, cancellation notice, or vendor confirmation, it cannot be established that only one of the two invoice scans was actually processed for payment rather than both.
notes: All core document types for a standard purchase-to-pay cycle are present and internally consistent: PO-1003 (2026-07-12, INR 70,800 incl. 10,800 tax) is referenced by both invoice scans, the goods receipt REC-1003 (2026-07-19), the bank debit BNK-1003 (2026-08-10), and the ledger entry LED-1003, all sharing the common reference SSS/2026/188 and matching total amount of 70,800 INR. The date sequence (PO -> invoice -> receipt -> payment -> ledger) is logical and amounts reconcile across documents. However, two invoice records (INV-1003-A and INV-1003-B) are identical in vendor, amount, tax, date, and references, explicitly flagged by intake as a likely duplicate scan of the same underlying supplier invoice. This duplication does not by itself prove double payment occurred, but it also is not proof that it did not - only a single bank debit (BNK-1003) and single ledger entry (LED-1003) are present, which is consistent with a single payment having been made, though this cannot be treated as definitive reconciliation absent explicit documentation tying the payment to exactly one of the two invoice scans. Additionally, tax_amount is not separately broken out in the bank statement, receipt, or ledger entry (all leave tax_amount null), so the 10,800 tax figure is only independently corroborated by the PO and the two invoice scans, not by downstream financial records. Confidence is moderated downward from a near-complete evidence set due to the unresolved duplicate invoice issue and the lack of separate tax substantiation in the payment/ledger trail.
